CONTROLLED KINETICS AROUND A SOLVABLE INTERACTING REFERENCE
Root construction, 1 November 2026

Status and scientific meaning
-----------------------------
This is a constructive mathematical result and a partially implemented algorithm.
It is not a demonstrated new material, a general molecular simulator, or an
established historical-priority claim. Its primitives have substantial prior art:
reversible return identities, free-fermion/matchgate contraction, preconditioned
inverse approximation, exponential sums, and tensor methods for absorption.

The particular synthesis constructed here evaluates scalar kinetic inverse moments
by finite words of local operators inserted into an interacting Gaussian reference.
It avoids requiring a compressible full solution vector. At fixed interaction
contrast, locality and requested accuracy, it has polynomial arithmetic work in
system size and in the logarithm of spectral stiffness. This is a more precise claim than
'rare events without waiting', which an ordinary target-start estimator also earns.
The constants and accuracy exponent are serious limitations, written below.

1. Physical model and input contract
-----------------------------------
There are n (even, n>=4) spins on a periodic chain with energy

    beta H(sigma) = -sum_i J_i sigma_i sigma_(i+1).

J_i in this note already includes beta. Couplings may have either sign. Local
attempt frequencies nu_i are strictly positive, finite, and explicitly supplied.
No unknown force law, measured response or equilibrating helper is supplied.
The service is a calculation from this exact model, not a measurement of a material.
For bit complexity, inputs have finite effective encodings with certified p-bit
evaluation cost polynomial in their encoded length and p. Arbitrary real-number
oracles are not admitted. Local rate tables and elementary functions of rational
encoded parameters can be evaluated under this contract.

Use domain walls eta_i=(1-sigma_i sigma_(i+1))/2. The wall count is even. Quotienting
the two global orientations gives exactly 2^(n-1) states. This lumping is exact for
zero-field spin flips. The target b is no domain walls: EITHER uniform orientation,
not a specified one of them. Adding a field or resolving global orientation requires
a different construction and is not silently covered.

FINAL MATHEMATICAL AUDIT OF ROOT PROOFS.txt
1 November 2026

Verdict
-------
The operator construction is mathematically sound under its stated common-Gibbs,
positive bounded-contrast assumptions. The scalar inverse theorem, the geometric
exponential-sum construction, and the centered-energy source extension survive
independent audit. The logarithmic-stiffness work statement also has a constructive
finite-precision route, provided the support-count, backward-error, phase-tracking,
and source-conditioning details below are included.

This is an audit of a theorem and a partially implemented algorithm. It does not
establish historical novelty, a conventional-algorithm lower bound, an end-to-end
directed-rounding implementation, or a large-system high-order performance result.
The successful target-start and multiscale competitors remain part of the decision.

1. Statements that pass
-----------------------
For the even wall-parity sector of the zero-field ring, the domain-wall heat-bath
rates and their symmetrization are correct. The free-fermion cancellation is the
identity a+c=d+e. The physical gap is the sum of the two lowest positive normal-mode
energies, not necessarily the lowest single-particle energy. The no-wall target is
the pair of globally aligned spin configurations after quotienting orientation.

An endpoint-invariant local multiplier A_i preserves detailed balance with the
same Gibbs law. Consequently m K0 <= K <= M K0 holds as an operator-form comparison.
Each COMPLETE local E_i annihilates the common ground vector. This property must
not be assigned to its individual Majorana monomials.

The return identity W/[pi_b(1-pi_b)] is correct for the specified equilibrium law
conditioned outside the target. It does not require preparing that distribution in
the computation. It also does not constitute a physical preparation protocol.

The sharp Neumann relative error is correct:

    |W_k-W| <= rho^(k+1) W.

The proof uses a positive scalar spectral measure, so it applies to any nonzero
source in the orthogonal complement of the stationary vector. The Chebyshev
polynomial and its relative scalar error are also correct. Treat rho=0 separately:
the perturbation vanishes after scalar recentering and the reference inverse alone
suffices. Expressions containing 1/rho should not be evaluated in that case.
